claim: Header frames Figure 1 as a Sun-Abraham (2021 JoE) staggered event study with leads/lags around a treatment time, `_first_treat = min(year if digital_frontier==1)` (line 33) and cohort(_first_treat) (line 68).
problem: digital_frontier is a time-invariant base-year group (runner.py:1138), not a staggered adoption event. For every frontier bank `_first_treat` equals the panel's first year, so all treated units share one cohort with no pre-period and no staggered variation; the never-treated set is the complement. The Sun-Abraham interaction-weighted cohort machinery has effectively zero cohort variation to exploit, and the 'event study' is really a single 2x(time) DiD on a fixed group. The graceful T=2 / cohort-degeneracy guards (lines 73-76) hide this, but the framing overstates what the design can deliver at full T=19. Not a crash, but a conceptual mismatch between the cited estimator and the actual treatment variable.
evidence: 30_figure1:33 `egen _first_treat = min(cond(digital_frontier==1, year, .))`; runner.py:1126 '组员资格跨年固定'; single-cohort consequence of a time-invariant group.
suggested_fix: Disclose that digital_frontier is a fixed cross-sectional group (no staggered timing) so this figure is a group-vs-time DiD, not a staggered event study; if a genuine event study is wanted, anchor relative time to a real time-varying treatment/policy date rather than to a base-year group indicator.
verifier_fix: In the header (lines 3-9) and Figure 1 note, disclose that digital_frontier is a time-invariant base-year cross-sectional group (runner.py:1138, _base_year_median_split, "组员资格跨年固定"), so _first_treat (line 33) collapses to the panel's first year for every treated bank → a single cohort, no pre-period leads (all _rel_time ≥ 0), and zero staggered variation even at full T=19. Consequently this figure is a fixed-group-vs-time DiD, not a Sun-Abraham staggered event study, and the header's "处理前各年系数≈0 / 平行趋势" claim (lines 5-6) cannot be produced as written. Either (a) reframe the title/note and drop the Sun-Abraham/eventstudyinteract cohort machinery in favor of plain group×time TWFE leads/lags relative to a real event date, or (b) if a genuine staggered event study is wanted, anchor _rel_time to an actual time-varying policy/treatment date the panel already builds (e.g. dcep_post/sandbox_post/depins_post year thresholds) rather than to the base-year digital_frontier group indicator.
verifier_note: Independently re-derived the ground truth. The finding's technical premise is exactly correct. (1) digital_frontier is constructed by pipeline/panel/runner.py:1138 via _base_year_median_split (runner.py:241-270), which splits banks ONCE on base-year (panel['year'].min()) median news coverage and broadcasts that 0/1 membership to all years — the docstring/comment state verbatim "组员资格跨年固定" (group membership fixed across years), and runner.py:1133-1136 documents this was a deliberate change FROM a time-varying split TO a fixed cross-sectional group to satisfy the pre-treatment fixed axiom. So digital_frontier is time-invariant, NOT a staggered adoption event. (2) Consequence in 30_figure1_event_study.do.tmpl:33: `egen _first_treat = min(cond(digital_frontier==1, year, .))` — because a frontier bank has digital_frontier==1 in every year, _first_treat = the panel's first year for EVERY treated bank → a single shared cohort with zero staggered variation. (3) Line 34 `_rel_time = year - _first_treat` is therefore ≥ 0 for all treated observations → no pre-period leads exist, so the header's advertised parallel-trends test (lines 5-6: "处理前各年的系数应接近 0 ... DiD 前提成立") is structurally unfulfillable. (4) The Sun-Abraham cohort(_first_treat)/control_cohort(_never_treat) IW machinery (lines 67-68) has no cohort heterogeneity to weight even at full T=19 — the degeneracy is structural, not just a T=2 artifact, though the T=2 guard at lines 73-76 masks it at runtime by silently falling back to plain TWFE lead/lag. This is a genuine conceptual mismatch between the cited estimator (Sun-Abraham 2021 staggered event study) and the actual treatment variable (a fixed base-year group). It is not a crash and not a wrong-variable reference (digital_frontier exists; the capture confirm at line 24 only guards existence, not the framing), so P2 (econometric-soundness / design-framing) is the correct severity — non-blocking but the header overstates what the design delivers.

Concretely, in the foreach loop at lines 264-267 track the family of each kept estimate and set the pattern to 1 only at the first column of each Panel that actually realizes: e.g. `local pat ""; local prevfam ""; foreach m of local stored { if strmatch("`m'","feA_*")|strmatch("`m'","feB_*")|strmatch("`m'","feC_*") { local models `models' `m'; local fam = substr("`m'",1,3); if "`fam'"!="`prevfam'" { local pat `pat' 1; local prevfam "`fam'" } else local pat `pat' 0 } }`, and also build a parallel `grp_titles` list adding the Panel title only when a new family first appears (so the number of group titles always equals the number of 1-flags = number of panels that actually have >=1 column). Note the finder's ROOT-CAUSE diagnosis ('version varies across rwolf installs') is imprecise -- the bug is deterministic on the installed version due to the single-vs-multi branch, not install variance. Stock-Yogo maximal-relative-bias critical values are defined only for over-identified models with >=3 instruments and are undefined for just-identified IV — so 'X% maximal bias' is the wrong Stock-Yogo concept for the dominant (just-identified LOO / Bartik / ctx) columns. The numeric 16.38 is the conventional single-IV rule-of-thumb so the practical guidance (read AR CI when KP F < 16.38) is sound; only the 'maximal bias' label is imprecise. Note this mislabel is systemic (also root 25_tableA6:266, benefit 25:199/255, substance 22), so it is a convention-level imprecision rather than an isolated typo.

Cross-file systemic: 25_tableA6_tone_iv_2sls.do.tmpl:266, benefit_society/25_tableA12_iv_2sls.do.tmpl:199.

claim: All main and heterogeneity regressions use vce(cluster bank_id year) two-way clustering and report cluster-robust SE as the headline inference ('Cluster-robust SE (bank+year two-way)').
problem: The year cluster dimension is far below the few-cluster threshold: on the full corpus G_year = 19 (2007-2025), on the disk panel G_year = 2 (T=2). Two-way clustering on a dimension with ~2-19 groups gives badly downward-biased SEs (Cameron & Miller 2015, JHR), and the heterogeneity panels further split the already-small sample into 5 tiers / 4 sub-periods, leaving a handful of bank-year obs per cell. (2) The method described (split first into independent chunks, embed each independently, mean-pool) is precisely the NAIVE chunking baseline that the Late Chunking paper argues AGAINST; Late Chunking embeds the full document first and chunks the token embeddings afterward. So the comment both renames the paper wrongly and attributes to it the opposite technique the code actually implements.

verifier_note: Both factual claims are correct after independent verification. (1) Citation title: I fetched arXiv:2409.04701 directly — its title is "Late Chunking: Contextual Chunk Embeddings Using Long-Context Embedding Models" (Günther, Mohr, Williams, Wang, Xiao; Jina AI, 2024). The docstring calls it "Early Chunking", which is an invented term, not the paper's title. (2) Method attribution: the docstring describes "先按固定 token 数切分为 K 个不重叠段, 各段独立嵌入后均值池化" (split first into independent non-overlapping segments, embed each separately, then mean-pool). The arXiv abstract explicitly states the paper argues AGAINST exactly this naive practice ("chunk embeddings created in this way can lose contextual information... resulting in sub-optimal representations") and proposes the opposite: embed the whole long document first, then chunk the token embeddings just before mean-pooling. The code at token_utils.py:61-67 implements the naive approach (encode whole text -> slice into independent non-overlapping token windows, no contextual/late step), which downstream policy_alignment.py:840 embeds per-chunk and mean-pools. So the docstring both renames the paper wrongly AND attributes to it the precise baseline that paper critiques. The method itself (naive fixed-window mean-pooling) is fine as code; only the label and citation are wrong. P1 is appropriate per the project's standing concern with citation-integrity errors leaking into manuscripts/codebook.
